speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help determine the cause, can you describe exactly how the sensation feels, such as whether the room seems to be spinning or if you feel faint?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the position-dependent nature of your vertigo suggests a problem in the inner ear. Has this dizziness ever been accompanied by hearing loss, tinnitus, or a ringing in your ears during the episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The clinical presentation of sudden, position-dependent vertigo without other neurological deficits or significant hearing loss is classic for BPPV. No further diagnostic tests are required at this time.
